REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- Objective: “to improve learning outcomes in primary education” (section 15).  
- Scope & components: 1) Improving Primary School Readiness (childcare & ECE); 2) Leveraging Cost‑Effective Solutions (targeted instruction, Early Grade Learning, EdTech); 3) Learning‑Enhancing Infrastructure (climate‑resilient classrooms, WASH); 4) Institutional Capacity (HRMIS, M&E); 5) Contingent Emergency Response (CERC) (sections 19‑45).  
- Delivery model: MoEYS is the implementing agency; oversight by a Project Steering Committee (PSC) and day‑to‑day management by a Project Management Unit (PMU) (Legal covenants, sections 48‑49).  
- Timeline: Expected approval 29‑Aug‑2025; closing 31‑Dec‑2030 (datasheet).  
- Budget: US$105 million total (US$100 million IDA credit + US$5 million ELP grant) (Financing summary).  
- Key stakeholders: Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC), MoEYS, Ministry of Economy & Finance, Ministry of Civil Service, Provincial/District Offices of Education, NGOs, development partners (UNICEF, FCDO, JSDF, etc.) (sections 46‑48).  
- External dependencies: climate‑related disasters, donor funding continuity, procurement regulations, ICT infrastructure, land acquisition.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  

| Category | Candidate risk | Evidence |
|----------|----------------|----------|
| technical | Failure of climate‑resilient construction to meet standards | “The designs for 60 childcare centers and 20 preschool buildings will incorporate climate‑resilient construction practices” (Component 1). |
| technical | ICT equipment may fail under extreme heat/humidity | “selecting ICT equipment designed to withstand extreme temperatures and humidity” (62). |
| technical | Scale‑up of targeted instruction (TaRL) may lose implementation fidelity | “targeted instruction is only being piloted in 2025, implying less information … for implementation at scale” (35). |
| technical | HRMIS modernization may encounter technical feasibility issues | “Progression to Phase 2 is conditional on Phase 1 results demonstrating quality and feasibility in terms of (a) technical and system development” (40‑41). |
| financial | FM staff overload causing transaction delays | “The current FM staff … may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting” (63a). |
| financial | Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) | “The delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may hinder the timely implementation of project activities” (63b). |
| financial | Inadequate monitoring of school‑mentoring funding | “There is a risk that school mentoring funding … may not be properly monitored” (63c). |
| stakeholder | Community resistance to childcare centres near factories | “The childcare centers will be developed … prioritizing areas near garment or industrial factories …” (23). |
| stakeholder | GBV data gaps limit effective interventions | “significant lack of comprehensive data on GBV prevalence … data focus on women ages 15 and above, not on primary school‑aged children” (57‑58). |
| political_regulatory | Failure to establish PSC/PMU as required by legal covenants | “The Recipient shall establish … a Project Steering Committee (PSC) … and shall maintain … a Project Management Unit (PMU)” (Legal covenants). |
| environmental | Land acquisition / involuntary resettlement issues (ESS 5) | “ESS 5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement – Relevant” (risk table). |
| environmental | Impacts on Indigenous peoples / traditional communities (ESS 7) | “ESS 7: Indigenous Peoples/... Traditional Local Communities – Relevant” (risk table). |
| organizational | PMU may lack sufficient resources for logistics & coordination | “The PMU will need additional resources for logistics, physical space, and transportation” (44). |
| external | Donor support (DPs) phasing out by 2027 may create funding gaps | “DPs … will phase out by 2027” (46). |
| external | CERC has zero budget; activation may be constrained | “Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response (CERC) (US$0 million)… objective … to allow for the reallocation of undisbursed financing …” (45). |
| procurement | Limited staff knowledge of World Bank procurement rules | “MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations …” (68a). |
| procurement | Governance risk of corrupt practices in procurement | “governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement” (68c). |
| schedule | Climate‑related school closures delay implementation | “Natural disasters … lead to prolonged school closures, loss of instructional time” (12). |
| schedule | Construction delays for climate‑resilient classrooms | “The subcomponent aims … to finance the climate‑resilient construction of additional classrooms” (37). |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly supported by quoted statements; none are discarded.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification | Mitigation |
|----|------------------|--------------|---------------|------------|
| R01 | 3 | 4 | Designs are planned but climate events are frequent; construction quality may vary. | Conduct third‑party verification of designs, embed quality‑assurance inspections, set contingency funds for remedial works. |
| R02 | 2 | 3 | Equipment specs address climate, but failures still possible. | Procure only certified climate‑rated ICT gear, include warranties and spare‑parts stock, pilot test in hot/humid sites. |
| R03 | 4 | 4 | Pilot limited to 2025; scaling nationwide historically reduces fidelity. | Deploy phased rollout with continuous monitoring, strengthen teacher coaching, use rapid‑learning cycles to adjust implementation. |
| R04 | 3 | 3 | Phase 2 depends on technical feasibility; system integration can be complex. | Perform thorough feasibility study, engage experienced IT vendor, pilot HRMIS in select districts before full deployment. |
| R05 | 3 | 3 | FM staff already noted as overloaded. | Recruit additional FM officers as planned, provide capacity‑building, streamline procedures with simplified AWPB templates. |
| R06 | 2 | 3 | AWPB approval is procedural but delays affect timing. | Set internal pre‑approval deadlines, prepare documentation early, monitor approval calendar. |
| R07 | 3 | 3 | Monitoring of mentoring funds is explicitly flagged as a risk. | Develop clear monitoring guidelines, conduct regular audits, publish quarterly mentoring‑fund reports. |
| R08 | 3 | 4 | Procurement knowledge gaps can cause non‑compliance and delays. | Provide targeted training on WB procurement rules, assign a dedicated procurement officer, use checklists. |
| R09 | 2 | 4 | Corruption risk is high‑impact though controls exist. | Enhance transparency (publish procurement plans, contract awards), establish a robust complaint mechanism, conduct random post‑reviews. |
| R10 | 4 | 4 | Climate disasters are frequent in Cambodia (floods, cyclones). | Build flexible timelines, integrate remote‑learning modules, maintain a contingency schedule for lost school days. |
| R11 | 3 | 3 | Large‑scale construction often faces delays. | Use fast‑track procurement, monitor progress with milestone payments, include penalty clauses for missed deadlines. |
| R12 | 2 | 2 | Community acceptance not yet tested; risk low. | Conduct early community engagement, awareness campaigns, involve local leaders in centre management. |
| R13 | 3 | 3 | Data gaps on GBV may limit targeting. | Strengthen GBV data collection within M&E, partner with NGOs for surveys, integrate findings into program design. |
| R14 | 2 | 4 | Legal covenants are mandatory; breach could halt project. | Ensure PSC and PMU are formally established by stipulated dates, assign oversight responsibility, conduct compliance audits. |
| R15 | 3 | 4 | Land acquisition can trigger resettlement disputes. | Carry out comprehensive ESIA, follow national resettlement guidelines, provide fair compensation and livelihood restoration. |
| R16 | 2 | 3 | Indigenous peoples relevance noted; impact moderate. | Implement Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework, ensure free, prior, and informed consent, involve representatives in design. |
| R17 | 3 | 3 | PMU resource needs are explicit. | Allocate sufficient budget for logistics, hire needed staff, provide training on coordination and reporting. |
| R18 | 3 | 3 | Donor phase‑out may leave funding gaps for EGL. | Secure additional financing early (government, private sector), explore co‑financing, adjust scaling pace if needed. |
| R19 | 2 | 4 | No budget for CERC could limit emergency response. | Finalize CERC manual, pre‑identify reallocation triggers, maintain a small contingency reserve within the IDA credit. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All risks are distinct; none duplicated. The register contains 19 material risks supported by the appraisal document.
